content.title: Stocks to Watch Tuesday Recap: Ford Motor, Broadcom, Lennar
content.summary: 🔎 Ford Motor (F): The automaker expects about $19.5 billion in charges as it scales back electric-vehicle ambitions and shifts focus to gas-powered and hybrid vehicles. Shares closed slightly higher but edged lower after hours.

content.title: These Stocks Moved the Most Today: Tesla, Pfizer, Humana, Circle, CoreWeave, Broadcom, IonQ, Ford, Navan, and More
content.summary: Stocks were mixed Tuesday as U.S. hiring in November was stronger than expected and the unemployment rate jumped to 4.6%.  Ford  was up 0.2%.  The auto maker announced a pivot toward hybrids and away from electric cars.

content.title: S&P 500 Health Care Stocks Sink With Time Running Out On ACA Subsidies
content.summary: Centene, the top ACA Marketplace insurer by membership, and HCA Healthcare, the largest U.S. hospital operator, are among S&P 500 laggards on Tuesday amid reports that House Speaker Mike Johnson won't allow a vote to renew expiring premium subsidies, but he may not have completely shut the door.  Politico reported that GOP moderates are still working feverishly to come up with a last-minute solution for renewing the ACA subsidies that can win House passage on Wednesday, despite long odds and contentious debates within the Republican caucus.  Humana, the biggest S&P 500 loser on Wednesday, is focused on Medicare Advantage and doesn't offer Affordable Care Act coverage.

content.title: Humana Names Former Amazon Executive Next Insurance President. The Stock Drops.
content.summary: Humana  stock was falling after the healthcare insurer announced the retirement of its current insurance president and reiterated guidance for this year.  Humana shares were down 2.4% in early trading Tuesday.  The company said Tuesday that George Renaudin, president of its insurance segment, will retire by the third quarter of 2026.

content.title: 3 HMO Stocks in Focus Despite Rising Medical Costs, Regulatory Pressures
content.summary: The Medical-HMO industry pursues growth through M&A and tech innovation, aided by easing interest rates, but faces headwinds from rising medical costs, regulatory shifts and a shortage of healthcare professionals. UNH, HUM and CNC are likely to navigate industry storms.

content.title: 2 Healthcare Stocks with Exciting Potential and 1 We Ignore
content.summary: From novel pharmaceuticals to telemedicine, most healthcare companies are on a mission to drive better patient outcomes. Players catalyzing medical advancements have benefited from elevated demand, which has supported the industry’s returns lately - over the past six months, healthcare stocks have gained 14.1%, nearly mirrorring the S&P 500.
